full_judgment:
18. It is stated that the respondent No. 2 as Appellate Officer did not admit the appeal on point of limitation. The respondent No. 2 in his observation stated that:- 

 is not barred by limitation. 

 limitation the appellate officer rejected the appeal by his order dated 26.04.2011. As against the said judgment and order this petitioner filed another class suit No. 10 of 2011 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka on 03.05.2011. 

 39. Learned Advocate further submits that the question of limitation has not been enquired by the respondent No. 3 while admitting the Salishi Case. The respondent No. 3 committed a serious error of law resulting in an error occasioning a failure of justice. The respondent No. 2 has also committed an error resulting in an error of law occasioning failure of justice in not admitting the appeal case on some flimsy ground. 

 44. He next submits that the question of limitation has not been enquired by the 

 defendant (this petitioner) and whether the Salishi Case was barred by limitation of 10 years, and whether the appeal was filed in time or not; all these matters in issue have not been discussed by the learned Judge. 

 57. On perusal of the impugned judgment and order of the learned Additional District Judge, 2" Court Dhaka. We find the learned Additional District Judge, 2" Court Dhaka, did not commit any error which resulted in an error occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned judgment. The learned Additional District Judge rightly affirmed the judgment and order dated 03.11.2013. The finding of the learned Judge is not contradictory the question of limitation has been rightly enquired into by the respondent No. 3 and rightly found the case is not maintainable as it is clearly held that even on receipt of the notice the petitioner who was defendant in the original case failed to appear in the hearing on number of occasions. Moreso, the learned Court clearly found that plaintiff earlier filed writ petition No. 1622 of 2001 before the Hon'ble High Court Division challenging the cancellation of the membership and also cancellation of plot in which a rule Nisi was issued and the writ petition was pending till 12.10.2010 on which date this Hon'ble Court rejected the writ petition on the ground of non maintainability of the writ petition. 

 58. Due to rejection of the writ petition the cause of action of the instant dispute case has arisen. The learned Court on due and on proper consideration of the materials and the points involved in the Shalishi dispute Case No. 47 of 2010 rejected the case on the finding that the case is not maintainable as the same is barred by limitation and also held that the impugned order had not been issued by a person as envisaged in sub-Article (5) of Article 102 of the Constitution and accordingly the rule issued in writ petition No. 1622 of 2001 was discharged as being not maintainable.
